target.title: Fix Claude same-dir account-switch history mis-attribution (#1886)
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes #1886: after `claude /login` switches accounts on the shared default `~/.claude`, CodexBar attributed the new account's plan-utilization usage to the **previous** account's history bucket.

Root cause: on background polls, Claude-Keychain access is gated off (correctly — #1848), so the credential cache serves the previous account's stale credential → stale `historyOwnerIdentifier` (SHA256 of the refresh token) → previous account's bucket. A user-initiated refresh self-corrects via the keychain freshness sync, so the mis-attribution is **background-only**.

## Live-measured behavior (Claude Code 2.1.201, macOS)
Verified on a real two-account `/login` switch:
- `Claude Code-credentials` keychain item is updated **in place** (createdAt unchanged, modifiedAt bumped, ACL preserved).
- `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is **not** rewritten (stays stale).
- `~/.claude.json` → `oauthAccount.accountUuid` updates immediately to the new account.

So `~/.claude.json` is the only always-fresh, prompt-free (plain file, never gated) signal of the active account in the background. This may also help #1823.

## Fix — gate-free identity corroboration, fail-closed
Completes the intent behind the currently-unused `corroboratingPersistentRefHash` slot **without relaxing any Keychain gate** (#1848 untouched):
- Prompt-free reader of `~/.claude.json` `oauthAccount.accountUuid`.
- Persisted `historyOwnerIdentifier -> accountUuid` map (UserDefaults; mirrors the limit-reset detector store).
- In `recordPlanUtilizationHistorySample`: a first sighting **on a user-initiated refresh** binds the owner to the active account; a **positive mismatch** quarantines the sample by nulling the owner upstream so the existing `detectorAccountKey == nil` no-write guard fires. Automatic recovery on the next user-initiated refresh.

The critical subtlety: a `nil` account key from the resolver does **not** quarantine — `setHistories(_, for: nil)` writes to the shared `unscoped` bucket. The only true no-write path is the `detectorAccountKey == nil` early return, so the fix nulls the owner upstream to make the detector key and resolver arg go nil in lockstep.

Deliberately does **not** honor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (the credential store that yields `historyOwnerIdentifier` is home-relative; the accountUuid side must resolve against the same home).

## Update: hardened the empty-map upgrade path (addresses the Codex + ClawSweeper P2)
The first review flagged that on the very first run after upgrading (map empty) with an existing owner-keyed bucket, a **background** poll after a switch could still bind the stale owner to the new UUID — poisoning the map. Fixed: the first-sighting binding is now **only created on a user-initiated refresh** (`ProviderInteractionContext.current == .userInitiated`), where the keychain freshness sync guarantees the served owner reflects the active account. Background polls still **honor** an existing binding (quarantine on mismatch) but never **create** one; an unmapped background read fails open with no persisted binding — so the map can never be poisoned.

**Documented limitation + why fail-open is the default (ClawSweeper option 2):** the safeguard **arms after the first user-initiated sample** on an account. A same-directory switch in the narrow window *before* that first user-initiated sample fails open (writes the sample, identical to pre-fix behavior) but never poisons the map. In normal use the map is warmed by any menu open / manual refresh before a switch.

We deliberately **fail open** rather than quarantine background first-sightings that already have history, because `shouldRecordPlanUtilizationHistory` records Claude history on **background** polls too — quarantining those would stall plan-utilization history for users who rely on the menu-bar text and rarely open the menu, turning a rare, self-healing contamination into a broad ongoing gap. The genuine regression this fix removes is the map-**poisoning**; the residual warm-up window is identical to pre-fix behavior. If maintainers prefer guaranteed no-contamination over uninterrupted background history, the quarantine variant (drop background first-sightings whose owner already has a scoped bucket) is a small follow-up — that's the product call in ClawSweeper's option 1 vs 2.

## Real-behavior proof (patched code, real identity data — prompt-free)
Ran the patched `recordPlanUtilizationHistorySample` against **real** identity data on a two-account machine (all plain-file reads, no Keychain prompts). Owner derived via the app's own formula from the real refresh token (token never printed); active account read live from the real `~/.claude.json`; account B's real `accountUuid` captured from the actual `/login` switch. Redacted transcript:

```
REAL owner  = a38040d6f99ca105…  (app-formula SHA256 of the real refresh token; token never printed)
REAL active accountUuid (~/.claude.json, live read) = bc1b8375…
REAL account-B accountUuid (captured switch)         = 86ab30ce…
bucket key for REAL owner = __claude_oauth__:b4d9f26acd7197da2…

---- Scenario A: armed quarantine ----
step 1 (user-initiated @A): map[owner]=bc1b8375, key_A present=true, unscoped empty=true
  [after step 1] REAL history buckets → account[__claude_oauth__:b4d9f26acd…] usedPercent series: [[30.0]]
step 2 (BACKGROUND stale @B): buckets unchanged=true, unscoped empty=true
  [after step 2 (stale background poll)] account[__claude_oauth__:b4d9f26acd…] usedPercent series: [[30.0]]
✅ stale background sample QUARANTINED (history unchanged, no unscoped leak)

---- Scenario B: empty-map upgrade, no poison ----
empty-map background sightings: map[owner]=nil, map[uuidB]=nil, map.count=0
✅ NO POISON: background reads never created a binding
```

The stale 90% background sample after the switch is **not** written to the old bucket (history stays `[[30.0]]`), does not leak to `unscoped`, and the empty-map upgrade path creates no binding (no poison).

## Tests
- `same dir account switch quarantines stale background credential`: A (user-initiated) → quarantines a stale-A sample served on a background poll while `~/.claude.json` = B (asserts `unscoped` stays empty) → recovers to B.
- `background first sighting does not poison the account map`: empty map + background sightings across a switch → asserts no `owner→uuid` binding is ever created (the P2 regression). Verified to fail if the trustworthy-read gate is removed.
- All existing Claude-identity + plan-utilization tests pass.

## Commands run
- `swift build` (debug) → Build complete
- `swift test --filter UsageStorePlanUtilizationClaudeIdentityTests` → 23 passed (incl. both regressions)
- `swift test --filter UsageStorePlanUtilizationTests` → 52 passed
- `make test` (full sharded suite, 47 shards) → all passed (exit 0)
- `make check` (SwiftFormat + SwiftLint `--strict`) → clean (0 violations / 1264 files)

## Notes
- No UI change (history bucketing only), so no screenshots.
- ClawSweeper cleared security ("does not add dependencies or relax Keychain gates, stores no raw token material").
